hero.title: UK Market Entry Services
hero.subtitle: From deciding whether the UK is the right market to building a sustainable local presence.

item1.question: Should we enter the UK?
item1.name: UK Market Validation
item1.whatItSolves: Chinese businesses often commit to channels or stock before knowing whether UK demand, pricing and competition actually support the move. This answers that question first.
item1.whoItIsFor: Manufacturers and brands considering the UK for the first time, without direct experience of the market.
item1.next: If the assessment supports moving forward, we move into the UK Market Entry Roadmap or a 30-Day Market Test, depending on how much certainty you already have.

item2.question: How should we enter?
item2.name: UK Market Entry Roadmap
item2.whatItSolves: Once there is a case for entering, businesses need a coordinated plan — not a list of disconnected decisions made under pressure.
item2.whoItIsFor: Businesses that have decided to enter the UK and need a structured plan before committing budget and resource.
item2.next: The roadmap becomes the reference plan for execution — either through a 30-Day Market Test or direct entry, depending on risk appetite.

item3.question: Can we validate the opportunity?
item3.name: 30-Day Market Test
item3.whatItSolves: Plans and research can only tell you so much. This tests the opportunity against real market behaviour before further investment.
item3.whoItIsFor: Businesses with a validated plan who want evidence — not assumptions — before scaling.
item3.next: Results determine whether to scale the channel, adjust the approach, or pause before further investment.

item4.question: How do we establish locally?
item4.name: Business & People Landing
item4.whatItSolves: A genuine UK presence requires more than a company number — it requires the right structure, and in some cases, people on the ground.
item4.whoItIsFor: Businesses ready to commit to a lasting UK presence, commercially and operationally.

deliverables.item4: Coordination with immigration advisors, where relevant

item4.next: Ongoing advisory support as the business establishes and grows its UK operations.

perspective.title: We start with the problem, not our services.
perspective.body1: Many market entry providers work outward from what they already offer — a warehouse operator sells fulfilment, an agency sells channel management, a formation service sells company registration. Each may be the right answer for some businesses. It is rarely the first question worth asking.
perspective.body2: We start differently: understanding what a business actually needs, then assembling the right combination of expertise — rather than defaulting to whatever happens to already be on offer.
